cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) promises that some standing there will see *the kingdom of Elohim (God) come with power*. Daniel's verse says what that kingdom is: dominion and glory given to the one Daniel saw in his vision, a kingdom for all peoples to serve, and *his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed*.
cards.member_phrase: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away
cards.member_sentence: Daniel says the dominion and kingdom given to the one he saw are everlasting and will not pass away or be destroyed.

cards.prose: Elijah stands on the mountain talking with Yahusha (Jesus), and Second Kings tells how he left the earth: *a chariot of fire, and horses of fire* parted him from Elisha, and *Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven*. The man carried up in the whirlwind is the one who now appears beside Moses.
cards.member_phrase: Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven
cards.member_sentence: Elijah did not die; a chariot of fire parted him from Elisha and he went up by a whirlwind into heaven.

cards.prose: Moses is the other one on the mountain, and Deuteronomy says how his life ended: he *died there in the land of Moab*, the servant of Yahuah (the LORD), by his word. The lawgiver and the prophet who went up in the whirlwind now stand together talking with the one both of them wrote toward.
cards.member_sentence: Moses died in the land of Moab by the word of Yahuah (the LORD), and now appears beside Elijah with Yahusha (Jesus).

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) says of John, *they have done unto him whatsoever they listed*. Jezebel's threat to Elijah is the same hatred toward the same kind of prophet, a message saying she will make his life *as the life of one of them* by tomorrow. The man who comes in Elijah's power meets what Elijah was threatened with.
cards.member_phrase: So let the gods do to me, and more also, if I make not thy life as the life of one of them
cards.member_sentence: Jezebel swears to take Elijah's life by the next day, the threat that the prophet in Elijah's power meets again in John.

cards.prose: Malachi promised that Yahuah (the LORD) would send Elijah the prophet before *the great and dreadful day of Yahuah (LORD)*. Yahusha (Jesus) says the one promised *is indeed come*, and means John, and adds that what was done to him was *written of him* too.
cards.member_sentence: Malachi promises Elijah the prophet before the great and dreadful day, the promise Yahusha (Jesus) says John fulfils.

cards.prose: What they did to John *whatsoever they listed* was done before to Zechariah the son of Jehoiada. The Spirit of Elohim (God) came on him and he stood above the people and asked, *Why transgress ye the commandments of Yahuah (LORD)*? The prophet who set the commandments before a people that had left them was the one they killed.
cards.member_phrase: Why transgress ye the commandments of Yahuah (LORD), that ye cannot prosper?
cards.member_sentence: Zechariah, filled by the Spirit of Elohim (God), told the people they had forsaken the commandments of Yahuah (the LORD).

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) counts the killing of the prophets in a line from Abel to a man slain *between the temple and the altar*. John, done to *whatsoever they listed*, stands in that line. Chronicles gives the dead prophet's father as Jehoiada where Matthew writes Barachias.
cards.member_phrase: from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zechariah son of Barachias
cards.member_sentence: Matthew counts the righteous blood from Abel to Zechariah, slain between the temple and the altar, as the line John stands in.
cards.flag: Chronicles names Zechariah's father Jehoiada, Matthew Barachias; left open, not reconciled in the card.

cards.prose: Right off the mountain, with the glory still on them, Yahusha (Jesus) tells them to say nothing *till the Son of Adam were risen from the dead*. Isaiah had already drawn what lies between the glory and the rising: a man *despised and rejected of men*, who knew sorrow and grief.
cards.member_phrase: He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah draws the man despised, rejected and acquainted with grief, the road that lies between the mountain and the rising.

cards.prose: *The Son of Adam is delivered into the hands of men*, he teaches the twelve, and Isaiah has the shape of it: *taken from prison and from judgment*, *cut off out of the land of the living*. The reason Isaiah gives is not his own doing: *for the transgression of my people was he stricken*.
cards.member_phrase: he was cut off out of the land of the living: for the transgression of my people was he stricken
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah says he was taken from prison and judgment and cut off from the living because of the transgression of my people.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) teaches that *they shall kill him*, and that he shall rise the third day. Zechariah has Yahuah (the LORD) call the sword *against my shepherd*, and what follows the smiting is the flock: *the sheep shall be scattered*.
cards.member_phrase: smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered: and I will turn mine hand upon the little ones
cards.member_sentence: Zechariah says the shepherd is smitten and the sheep are scattered, with the hand turned upon the little ones.

cards.prose: To receive a child *in my name*, says Yahusha (Jesus), is to receive him, and to receive him is to receive the Father who sent him. Matthew gives the household the same test: whoever does *the will of my Father which is in heaven* is brother, sister and mother. The family is known by the doing.
cards.member_sentence: Matthew says whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is brother, sister and mother to Yahusha (Jesus).

cards.prose: The same chain runs through both books: the one who receives the one sent receives the sender. Mark has it at a child, *receiveth me: and whosoever shall receive me, receiveth not me, but him that sent me*. John has Yahusha (Jesus) say it of those he sends out, so a sent one's welcome rests on the same word as a child's.
cards.member_sentence: John says whoever receives the one Yahusha (Jesus) sends receives him, and receives the Father who sent him.

new_threads.title: The Son of Adam must suffer and be killed — despised, taken from judgment, the shepherd smitten
new_threads.summary_md:
It ain't new. Coming down from the mountain with the glory still on them, Yahusha (Jesus) tells the three to hold their tongues until the rising.

*And as they came down from the mountain, he charged them that they should tell no man what things they had seen, till the Son of Adam were risen from the dead.* (Mark 9:9)

What lies between the glory and the rising had been written already, in the picture of a man the people would not own.

*He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief: and we hid as it were our faces from him; he was despised, and we esteemed him not.* (Isaiah 53:3)

Then, passing through Galilee, he stops hinting and teaches the twelve plainly.

*For he taught his disciples, and said unto them, The Son of Adam is delivered into the hands of men, and they shall kill him; and after that he is killed, he shall rise the third day.* (Mark 9:31)

Isaiah has the same road, and says whose transgression stands behind it.

*He was taken from prison and from judgment: and who shall declare his generation? for he was cut off out of the land of the living: for the transgression of my people was he stricken.* (Isaiah 53:8)

Zechariah has the flock's side of it, the shepherd smitten by the sword Yahuah (the LORD) of hosts calls up, and the sheep scattering after.

*Awake, O sword, against my shepherd, and against the man that is my fellow, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts): smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered: and I will turn mine hand upon the little ones.* (Zechariah 13:7)

So when Mark says the twelve *understood not that saying*, the fault was not that the saying was new. The despised man, the one taken from judgment and cut off from the living, and the shepherd with the scattering flock were already on the page they had been reading all their lives.
